title: Illustrative Examples of LHmom
text: vignette demonstrates core functionalities LHmom package using built-bangkok dataset. dataset contains annual maximum series daily rainfall Bangkok, Thailand, 1951 2025. walk process calculating sample LH-moments, estimating parameters Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) distribution, evaluating model fit.

title: Illustrative Examples of LHmom
text: can install development version LHmom GitHub :

title: Illustrative Examples of LHmom
text: Load package dataset:
code: library(LHmom) data(bangkok1)  # View the first few rows head(bangkok1) #>   year rainfall #> 1 1951    133.5 #> 2 1952    111.0 #> 3 1953     84.1 #> 4 1954     53.8 #> 5 1955    108.8 #> 6 1956     69.4

title: Illustrative Examples of LHmom
text: Users can compute sample LH-moments given order η\eta subsequently estimate parameters various distributions. following example demonstrates fitting GEV distribution using first order LH-moments (η=1\eta = 1).

title: Illustrative Examples of LHmom
code: # Calculate sample LH-moments at eta = 1 sample_lh <- lhmoms(bangkok1$rainfall, eta = 1) print(sample_lh$lambdas) #>        lhmom-1  lhmom-2  lhmom-3  lhmom-4  lhmom-5 #> eta=1 126.5447 18.86068 5.220361 3.037946 1.666922

title: Illustrative Examples of LHmom
text: Next, estimate GEV parameters using calculated sample LH-moments:
code: # Estimate GEV parameters (eta = 1) fit_gev <- lh.pargev(bangkok1$rainfall, eta = 1) print(fit_gev$para) #>          xi       alpha           k  #> 87.64384852 28.23812277 -0.06139394

title: Illustrative Examples of LHmom
text: verify estimation algorithm, can calculate theoretical LH-moments newly fitted parameters: Notice numerical consistency: GEV three-parameter distribution, estimation algorithm successfully equates first three sample LH-moments theoretical counterparts.
code: # Calculate theoretical LH-moments from the fitted parameters theo_lh <- lhmom.gev(fit_gev$para, eta = 1) print(theo_lh$lambdas) #>    LHmom-1    LHmom-2    LHmom-3    LHmom-4  #> 126.544685  18.860680   5.229035   3.131879

title: Illustrative Examples of LHmom
text: crucial aspect extreme value analysis model validation. wang.test.lhgev() function evaluates whether GEV distribution provides suitable fit data across different LH-moment orders (η\eta) calculating Z-statistic based difference sample theoretical LH-kurtosis.

title: Illustrative Examples of LHmom
text: results demonstrate satisfactory fit across η\eta values, pp-values significantly exceed 0.05 significance level. Notably, η=3\eta = 3, absolute Z-statistic reaches minimum, pp-value approaches unity. indicates employing higher-order LH-moment (η=3\eta = 3) captures upper-tail distributional shape annual maximum rainfall exceptionally well compared ordinary L-moments (η=0\eta = 0).

title: LHmom: Higher-order L-Moment Estimation
text: LHmom package provides comprehensive framework parameter estimation using higher-order L-moments (LH-moments). assigning greater weight upper-tail observations, LH-moments offer robust statistical method extreme value analysis, particularly hydrological atmospheric research. Furthermore, design, parameterization, output structures package closely follow style conventions widely used lmomco package. ensures familiar, seamless, consistent interface users already accustomed standard L-moment calculations R.

title: LHmom: Higher-order L-Moment Estimation
text: Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) Generalized Pareto (GPA) Generalized Logistic (GLO) Generalized Normal (GNO) Pearson Type III (PE3) Gumbel (GUM) Generalized Gumbel (GGD) Three-parameter Kappa (fixed kk hh) Highly flexible Four-parameter Kappa (KAP) Diagnostic Tools: Includes universal Quantile-Quantile (Q-Q) plotting visual goodness--fit validation explicit implementation Wang’s goodness--fit test GEV distribution. Built-Datasets: Includes historical environmental datasets (bangkok1, khonkaen, sarakham) immediate demonstration flood frequency extreme climatic event modeling.

title: LHmom: Higher-order L-Moment Estimation
text: can install development version LHmom GitHub using devtools package:
code: # Install devtools if not already installed if (!require("devtools")) install.packages("devtools")  # Install LHmom from GitHub devtools::install_github("palakorn-seenoi/LHmom")

title: LHmom: Higher-order L-Moment Estimation
text: basic workflow using built-bangkok1 dataset estimate parameters Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) distribution using first order LH-moments (eta = 1):
code: library(LHmom)  # Load the built-in annual maximum rainfall dataset data(bangkok1)  # 1. Calculate sample LH-moments at eta = 1 sample_lh <- lhmoms(bangkok1$rainfall, eta = 1) print(sample_lh$lambdas)  # 2. Estimate GEV parameters using sample LH-moments fit_gev <- lh.pargev(bangkok1$rainfall, eta = 1) print(fit_gev$para)  # 3. Generate Q-Q plot with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals lh.qqplot(bangkok1$rainfall, fit_gev,            main = "GEV Q-Q Plot (eta = 1)",            ci = TRUE, ci_level = 0.95)  # 4. Perform Wang's goodness-of-fit test for the GEV distribution wang.test.lhgev(bangkok1$rainfall)

title: Estimate Parameters of the Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) Distribution using LH-moments — lh.pargev
text: function estimates parameters Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) distribution based sample LH-moments. estimation methodology follows Wang (1997). provides two approaches estimating shape parameter: using Wang's predefined polynomial approximations utilizing numerical optimization.

title: Estimate Parameters of the Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) Distribution using LH-moments — lh.pargev
Estimate Parameters of the Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) Distribution using LH-moments — lh.pargev
text: data numeric vector data values. eta non-negative integer (0 4) representing order LH-moments. Default 1. opt logical value indicating estimation method shape parameter. FALSE (default), uses Wang's polynomial approximation coefficients. TRUE, uses numerical optimization via nleqslv. ntry integer specifying maximum number initialization attempts numerical optimization solver opt = TRUE. Default 5.

title: Estimate Parameters of the Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) Distribution using LH-moments — lh.pargev
text: list containing: type: distribution type ("gev"). para: named numeric vector containing estimated parameters (xi location, alpha scale, k shape). eta: order LH-moments used. source: name function ("lh.pargev"). ifail: numeric indicator optimization solver's status (0 success, 5 failure converge).
